correctness.rationale: The source uses total (independent-set-complement) rather than ordinary (disconnected-set-complement) cut convention. Independently enumerated exactly 32 edges, 208 independent triples, 64670 nonempty faces and stated full 13-entry f-vector; sequential vertex matching generated 32270 pairs, one critical vertex and 129 critical 10-faces. Independent complete topological sort traversed 64670 vertices and 513248 Hasse covers, establishing Forman acyclicity and the integral 129-sphere wedge; purity dimension 12 then obstructs shelling. A separate independently coded Alexander-dual trace enumerator formed all 865 bounded-independence faces and calculated every one of 384 automorphism traces in the 20 signed-cycle types, matching every claimed class size and trace (identity 129). B4 automorphisms are even permutations of the 16 vertices, avoiding Alexander-duality sign twists. The finite exhaustive proof applies exactly to Q4 and does not claim all hypercube dimensions.
residual_risks: An unindexed older B4-equivariant homology or hypercube total cut result could cover the character.
The non-equivariant wedge is potentially reconstructible from a later published general BI3 lemma; its originality cannot be claimed solely from the number 129.
No all-n hypercube classification or canonical B4 module basis follows.

evidence: Bayer et al. address complete-bipartite, chordal and select path-product graph families; Q4 is not complete bipartite nor P2/P3 x Pn. A later published Möbius-ladder proof contains a general 2-connectivity lemma for BI3 on connected graphs; combined with cube-specific elementary face enumeration it could also imply the nonequivariant 129-sphere wedge, but it postdates this Q4 record and does NOT imply the 20-class character.
